description:
The /fly HUD speed readout shows 'NaN km/s' for outer-planet destinations (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres, etc.) throughout the entire flight.

Expected: The speed readout should show a realistic heliocentric speed value (km/s) for the spacecraft's current position on the transfer arc, regardless of destination.

Acceptance criteria:
- The heliocentric speed readout for a Jupiter mission (e.g. Galileo, Juno) at r ≈ 1 AU (near Earth departure) must be a finite number close to ~38-42 km/s (typical Earth departure speed for a Jupiter transfer). [repo-data: static/data/planets.json: Jupiter a=5.20336; the Hohmann transfer a = (1.0 + 5.2)/2 = 3.1 AU, vis-viva at r=1 AU gives v = sqrt(4π²·(2/1 − 1/3.1))·4.7404 ≈ 40.1 km/s]
- The speed readout for an outer-planet mission must never show NaN, Infinity, or any non-numeric string for any value of scR within the mission's arc (0 ≤ scR ≤ ~2·dest_a). [code-invariant: Math.sqrt of a negative radicand is a crash-level API misuse — the app must not produce NaN in a user-facing readout]
- The existing Mars mission speed readout must remain unchanged (same numeric value as before the fix). [baseline: The current behavior for Mars missions is the expected correct window; Mercury/Venus missions (inner planets) must also produce finite values]
